findings.body: Every caller that observed the initial miss subsequently acquires the exclusive lock and rereads and reparses the same manifest, creating a serialized cold-start lock convoy and increasing request latency and disk I/O under startup traffic.
findings.failure_mode: Concurrent cache misses are serialized into redundant manifest loads instead of being coalesced into one initialization.
findings.impact: Every caller that observed the initial miss subsequently acquires the exclusive lock and rereads and reparses the same manifest, creating a serialized cold-start lock convoy and increasing request latency and disk I/O under startup traffic.
findings.root_cause: The pre-lock cache value in ret is stale after waiting for the write lock, but the code does not validate the cache again inside the critical section.
findings.suggested_fix: After acquiring the write lock, recheck entryPointAssetsCache for non-development environments and return it immediately if another caller initialized it while this caller was waiting.
findings.title: Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.trigger: When multiple non-development requests enter GetWebAssets concurrently while the cache is empty, more than one caller can observe nil before the first caller acquires and releases the write lock.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch introduces a classic double-checked locking pattern without the second check. Lines 41-47 read cache under RLock, then line 48 acquires Lock without rechecking entryPointAssetsCache. Multiple goroutines observing nil before the first Lock acquisition will each proceed to re-read and re-parse the manifest serially. The cited line 48 exists verbatim, the cause is introduced by this patch, the trigger (concurrent cold-cache requests) is realistic for startup traffic, and the impact (redundant manifest loads causing latency) follows logically.
